comments.text:
There's definitely going to be mass unemployment in the next decade, but I don't think it will displace most people in that time. I suspect instead, what we will see is an averaging effect on salaries as AI makes ALL jobs easier to do, and thus lowers the bar of entry into those positions. A high priced lawyer could be replaced by a charismatic person with an AI device whispering in their ear for example, or a senior level software developer could be replaced by a kid with a couple of months of coding experience and be just as good (minus the designing capabilities).
This will have the net effect of averaging wages across the board. Lower positions will make more and higher paying positions will make less. This is what concerns me most about this transition to a post-labor economy. At this point, the gap between the middle class and the upper class will peel away like an old Band-Aid. The upper middle class will likely lose their homes and cars as they will no longer be able to make ends meet. That widespread defaulting on loans will cripple the financial institutions, and you'll see massive bank failures like we did in 2008.

comments.text: All of these claims that keep coming out about AGI/ASI will seem much more credible once any of these so called AIs can accomplish literally even one of the tasks I have tasked them with. I've not had one single LLM or image generation model successfully complete one single task I have set, in any test. The pattern is always the same. I first describe the desired task and ask the model if it is capable of completing that sort of work. It confidently gives a detailed response about how it absolutely is capable of completing the task. I give it the task. It fails miserably, or just flat does not remotely attempt it and gives lies in an attempt to fake doing the task. I give detailed feedback about how the model has failed to complete/attempt the task. The model either gives the same wrong response again, a slightly adjusted but still completely wrong response that doesn't even address the issues I brought up, or modifies its lie to attempt to fake that it has understood the problem and is working to actually perform the task this time. Rinse and repeat. No task I've asked for is sufficiently complex to require more than four sentences (maximum) to describe to the model. More verbose explanations with multiple redundancies (explaining with multiple methods to aid in understanding) result in zero improvement. When not attempting tasks, but rather asking for simple information about math (because I figured that would be the hardest topic to fuck up, given that there are well documented single correct answers to the questions I ask) models consistently give confidently incorrect answers.
